verdict.rationale: The evidence pack never documents parallel steps, fan-out/fan-in over dynamic batches, or child workflows that a parent waits on. The closest items are generic: tasks can be triggered and return a handle for status, cancel, and retry, and workflows are written in plain async code. Those are building blocks a developer could hand-roll coordination from, not the composition capability itself, so they earn no credit.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I compose workflows from parallel steps, fan-out/fan-in over dynamic batches, and child workflows without hand-rolling coordination
